data.description_html:
Ben jij een klantvriendelijke, administratieve topper met een no-nonsense mentaliteit en een hoog verantwoordelijkheidsgevoel? Stap in en versnel mee als Dealer Finance Specialist!

Over de rol

Als Dealer Finance Specialist ben je het eerste aanspreekpunt voor dealers die klant zijn óf dat willen worden. Je geeft uitleg over het product om te bepalen of Hiltermann en de potentiële klant bij elkaar passen. Als dat zo is, ben je verantwoordelijk voor het compleet maken en houden van het dossier. Nadat de klant live is gezet, ben je verantwoordelijk voor het dagelijkse beheer van deze klant rondom Voorraadfinanciering.

Jouw dagelijkse werkzaamheden omvatten: 

  • Voeren van intake gesprekken voor product en systeem uitleg en bepalen fit Hiltermann en dealer;

  • Uitzetten én monitoren van (potentiële) klanten voor mogelijke aanvullende samenwerkingen binnen het Hiltermann concern;

  • Behandelen van uitval uit de processen en toelichting geven aan onze klanten;

  • Toepassen verhoogde dijkbewaking bij Bijzonder Beheer klanten, zoals het treffen van betaalregelingen en het voorkomen en oplossen van storno's; 

  • Uitzetten voorraadcontroles, monitoren terugkomst resultaten en gepaste actie nemen richting klanten indien nodig. Ondersteuning van klanten (vaak bij hen op locatie) bij de onboarding; 

  • Verwerken van directiebesluiten rondom aanvragen en opstellen van diverse financieringsovereenkomsten; 

  • Controle op maand en kwartaalafsluitingen; 

  • Bijdragen aan procesverbeteringen, maken van procesbeschrijvingen en handleidingen;

  • Bezoeken van klanten (1 dag per week tot 1 dag per 2 weken). 

Over jou

Je bent klantvriendelijk, oplossingsgericht en administratief sterk. Daarnaast ben je een netwerker of wil je deze vaardigheid verder ontwikkelen. 

Verder heb jij: 

  • MBO+/HBO-denk en werkniveau; 

  • Ervaring in Automotive, ervaring in voorraadfinanciering is een pré; 

  • Goede kennis van Microsoft Office; 

  • Sterke administratieve vaardigheden; 

  • Flexibele en stressbestendige instelling. 

Wat bieden wij jou?  
Goed werk verdient een eerlijke beloning. Daarom bieden we bij Hiltermann Lease aantrekkelijke arbeidsvoorwaarden:

  • Een salaris tussen de €2.900,- en €4.000,-bruto per maand (o.b.v. een 40-urige werkweek), afhankelijk van jouw ervaring;

  • Een jaarcontract met de intentie om dit om te zetten in een vast contract bij gebleken geschiktheid;

  • 28 vakantiedagen (o.b.v. een 40-urige werkweek);

  • Een pensioenregeling met slechts 3% eigen bijdrage, waardoor je meer nettoloon overhoudt!

  • €30 netto per maand thuiswerkvergoeding (o.b.v. 40 u.p.w.);

  • Dagelijkse verse lunch op kantoor zonder eigen bijdrage;

  • Volledige vergoeding van OV-kosten als je met de trein of bus reist;

  • Reiskostenvergoeding van €0,23 per kilometer als je met de auto of fiets komt;

  • Hybride werken.


Enthousiast geworden?

Word dan onze nieuwe collega! Solliciteer via onderstaande sollicitatieknop. Binnen 3 werkdagen nemen wij contact met je op. Wil je meer weten over deze leuke job, lees dan vooral het verhaal van collega Dionne:

Dionne Groot| Medewerkersverhaal

The salary for this role is £57,117 (inclusive of a Specialist Allowance) Onsite working is expected for 4-5 days each week, however, we consider requests for flexible working, according to business needs. 

This role will be based at  Culham, Oxfordshire, but there may be occasional travel to other sites.

 

This role requires employees to complete an online Baseline Personnel Security Standard (BPSS), including The Disclosure & Barring Service (DBS) checks for criminal convictions and possibly a search of open source data. 

 

The Role

UKAEA’s centre for Remote Applications in Challenging Environments (RACE) specialises in designing, building, and operating robotic systems for extreme industrial environments.  As the RACE Electrical Quality Systems Team Leader, you will be responsible for ensuring the quality of all electrical manufacturing and installation activities across the RACE portfolio. You will create and manage Quality Management Plans, ensuring compliance with relevant international standards and requirements.

You will provide technical leadership in the design, approval and delivery of control panels, cubicles, operational systems and equipment. This will include supporting new projects through the design, modification, build and commissioning stages, requiring a practical and hands-on approach.

Responsibilities:

  • Lead and manage the Electrical Quality Team, providing line management, coaching and support to team members, while defining standards and promoting best working practices.
  • Own quality assurance across electrical systems within the RACE portfolio, including leading inspections, approving manufacturing quality and documentation from suppliers and contractors, and ensuring compliance with relevant international regulations, including Machinery and Low Voltage Directives.
  • Develop and maintain Quality Management plans, test plans and QA documentation, leading engineers and technicians through quality processes and ensuring a right-first-time approach through continuous improvement.
  • Provide technical leadership throughout the design, build, testing and commissioning lifecycle, participating in design reviews, advising Electrical Engineers on hardware manufacturability, and ensuring systems meet UKAEA site requirements and legislative safety standards.
  • Manage suppliers, subcontractors and external partners, including defining requirements, monitoring performance, leading supplier inspections and ensuring successful delivery of electrical systems to agreed quality, cost and schedule requirements.
  • Support project delivery and continuous technical development, collaborating with project managers on project planning, cost and timescale estimates, maintaining technical knowledge, updating documentation and ensuring effective Health & Safety management.

Essential:

  • Engineering qualification or equivalent experience, such as an Engineering degree, HNC/HND, or relevant practical experience, with extensive electrical engineering QA experience and the ability to assess electrical design work.
  • Strong technical knowledge of electrical engineering principles, including electrical machinery, distribution systems, relevant electrical quality standards, governance, Health & Safety requirements and compliance obligations.
  • Proven experience delivering electrical engineering projects, with a good understanding of project lifecycles and the ability to produce high-quality work within agreed deadlines.
  • Strong communication and collaboration skills, with experience working in cross-functional teams and the ability to interact effectively with people in a variety of situations.
  • A flexible and proactive approach to work, with the ability to work independently or as part of a team, support continuous improvement, and coach less experienced staff.

Desirable:

  • Experience of working in a safety-dominated working environment.
  • Experience in people management.

data.description_html:
Independent Non-Executive Director (Resident), Seychelles
 
About OKX
At OKX, we believe that the future will be reshaped by crypto, and ultimately contribute to every individual's freedom. OKX is a leading crypto exchange, and the developer of OKX Wallet, giving millions access to crypto trading and decentralized crypto applications (dApps). OKX is also a trusted brand by hundreds of large institutions seeking access to crypto markets. We are safe and reliable, backed by our Proof of Reserves. Across our multiple offices globally, we are united by our core principles: We Before Me, Do the Right Thing, and Get Things Done. These shared values drive our culture, shape our processes, and foster a friendly, rewarding, and diverse environment for every OK-er. OKX is part of OKG, a group that brings the value of Blockchain to users around the world, through our leading products OKX, OKX Wallet, OKLink and more.
Our Seychelles business has operated since 2017 and now sits within the licensing regime established by the Virtual Asset Service Providers Act of Seychelles 2024 (the VASP Act). We are seeking an Independent Non-Executive Director, resident in Seychelles, to join the board of our Seychelles entity to supplement its board of governance with an independent resident non-executive director.

About the Role
As an Independent Non-Executive Director and Resident Director of our Seychelles entity, you will bring independent challenge to strategy, risk and conduct, hold management to account on behalf of shareholders and stakeholders, and provide the resident board presence that the licence and the entity's governance arrangements require. The role exists to do three things at once: provide independent challenge; satisfy the Seychelles Financial Services Authority (the FSA) that the board of the Company meets its expectations on composition, competence and fitness and propriety under the VASP Act; and provide local substance in Seychelles.
The entity operates within the group's global governance, risk and compliance framework while remaining separately accountable to its own board and to its regulator. The Board comprises a mix of executive and independent non-executive directors. This is a genuinely resident role. The appointee must be physically present in Seychelles, attend board and management meetings in person, and be available to engage with the FSA and the entity's advisers in Seychelles.
A non-executive director carries the same general legal responsibilities to the entity as any other director, and must perform those duties faithfully, efficiently and diligently to a standard commensurate with the role and with their own knowledge, skills and experience.

What You’ll Be Doing
Independentally Challenge
  • Bring an external and independent perspective to strategy, risk and conduct, and hold management to account on behalf of shareholders and stakeholders.
  • Provide constructive challenge and strategic guidance, and offer specialist advice to the Board.
  • Scrutinise the performance of management and of individual executive directors against agreed goals, and monitor how that performance is reported.
  • Act in good faith, honestly and responsibly, and make decisions objectively in what you consider to be the interests of the entity.
Regulatory Standing & Local Substance
  • Satisfy the FSA that the board of the Company meets its expectations on composition, competence and fitness and propriety under the VASP Act.
  • Provide the physical, resident board presence in Seychelles that the licence and the entity's governance arrangements require.
  • Attend board and management meetings in person, and engage with the FSA and the entity's advisers in Seychelles as required.
Collective Board Responsibilities
  • Promote the long term sustainable success of the entity, generating value for shareholders and contributing to wider society.
  • Establish the entity's purpose, values and strategy, and satisfy the Board that its culture is aligned to them.
  • Provide effective, prudent and ethical oversight, act with integrity, lead by example and promote the desired culture.
  • Ensure the resources needed to meet the entity's objectives are in place, and measure performance against them.
  • Establish and lead within a framework of prudent and effective controls that allows risk to be assessed and managed.
  • Ensure effective engagement with shareholders and stakeholders.
  • Ensure workforce policies and practices are consistent with the entity's values.
Individual Director Responsibilities
  • Satisfy yourself on the integrity of the entity's financial information, its financial controls, and whether its risk management systems are robust and defensible.
  • Determine appropriate remuneration for executive directors, and play a leading part in appointing and, where necessary, removing them.
  • Contribute to the entity's succession planning.
  • Uphold the highest standards of integrity, and support the chairperson in setting the values, behaviours and culture of the boardroom and beyond.
Committee Service
Serve on one or more board committees where required. The relevant terms of reference will be provided on appointment.

What We Look for in You
  • Resident in Seychelles, and currently holding the right to reside and work there.
  • Able to satisfy the FSA's fitness and propriety assessment.
  • Board level or senior governance experience in a regulated financial services, banking, insurance, fiduciary or corporate services business.
  • Working knowledge of anti-money laundering and counter terrorist financing obligations, and of the Seychelles regulatory environment.
  • Financial literacy sufficient to interrogate financial statements, controls and risk reporting without support.
  • Demonstrable independence of mind, and the willingness to challenge management and record dissent.
  • Fluent in English, with excellent communication and stakeholder management abilities.
What Will Make You Stand Out
  • Experience of virtual assets, fintech, payments or capital markets.
  • Prior regulatory experience.
  • Experience chairing an audit, risk or compliance committee.
  • Experience of a group structure where much of the operating activity sits outside the licensed entity's jurisdiction, and of the oversight challenge that creates.
  • An established local network among Seychelles regulators, professional advisers and the financial services community.
 
Why Join OKX?
  • Play a pivotal role in the governance of a successful virtual asset business.
  • Bring independent oversight to a global crypto platform operating at scale across multiple jurisdictions.
  • Work alongside an experienced board and a global leadership team in a high-growth industry.

This position is with Manifest Global, which also includes trailblazer brands such as Cialfo, Explore, BridgeU, FlowAI, Kaaiser and Edugo.

What This Role Is

Most recruiters spend their careers fighting the same fight: a broken ATS, manual screening that eats the whole day, a hiring manager who ghosts the scorecard, a pipeline that starts from zero every time a req opens. That fight is largely over at Manifest. Resume screening, first-round AI phone screening, and interview scheduling already run on a live automation pipeline. Every open role carries a structured AI-Lens score before a hire is made. The administrative weight that usually defines a recruiter's day is already handled.

What's left is the part of the job that actually matters, and the part most recruiters never get enough time to do well: reading a role correctly before you source for it, building a pipeline before the req is desperate, coaching a hiring manager through a real interview instead of a rubber stamp, and closing a candidate who has other offers on the table. That's this role. You inherit a portfolio of open roles across the Manifest brand family, and you own each one end to end, inside a system built to let you spend your time on judgment, not logistics.

You own proving that a recruiter given real leverage, real tools, and real ownership can outperform a much bigger team running the old way.

What Makes This Role Different

Most Senior Talent Acquisition roles ask you to either inherit chaos or build infrastructure from nothing. This one asks something rarer: step into a function that's already operating ahead of where most companies' TA teams will be in a few years, and bring the craft that no automation stack can replace. If your best days as a recruiter are the ones spent actually talking to people, reading a candidate's real motivation, coaching a hiring manager into asking a better question, this is a role built around giving you more of those days, not fewer.

The Manifest ecosystem means your work isn't confined to one brand's hiring needs in isolation. You're building pipelines across a group actively investing in never starting critical searches from a blank page again, and the muscle you build here compounds across every brand you touch, not just one.

What You Own

Your portfolio of open roles, assigned as you join, owned end to end and tracked against a tiered service standard that separates urgent hires from foundational ones

Calibration and pipeline quality on every role you run: structured scorecards, AI-Lens scoring, and honest debate on any candidate who raises a real question, never a quiet pass or fail

Hiring manager partnership, coaching certified managers through structured interviewing and treating your own read on a role as something worth defending, not just executing

Pipeline building on the roles Manifest hires for again and again, so the next opening in your portfolio starts with a warm pool, not a cold search

Candidate experience on everything you touch, every applicant treated like their eventual review of Manifest matters, because it does

What Success Looks Like

The markers below reflect where the function is today. We'll calibrate the specifics to your actual portfolio once you're in the seat. These are directional, not fixed.

In the first weeks, you're ramped on your assigned roles and already a real contributor to how the function reads its own performance, not still learning the tools while roles sit open.

By mid-period, your roles are closing at a pace that reflects real calibration, your hiring managers trust your judgment enough to move fast on your recommendation, and at least one of your searches started from a pipeline you built before the req opened, not after.

In the long term, you're one of the people other recruiters and hiring managers point to when they want to see what good calibration actually looks like, and your portfolio is proof the system works because of the person running it, not just the automation underneath it.

The specifics will be calibrated once you're in the role. The direction won't change.

What You Bring

You've recruited at real volume before, across more than a handful of roles at once, and you know the difference between a candidate who looks good on paper and one who'll actually close. You're coachable, genuinely energized by stepping into a system someone else designed well, rather than needing to rebuild it your way before you can do good work.

You're fluent in using AI tools in your own recruiting practice, not just aware that AI-native recruiting exists. You've screened, scored, or sourced with AI tools directly, and you light up talking about what changed when you did.

You're comfortable with a little ambiguity at the start. Your exact portfolio isn't fixed until you join, and you'd rather find out and move than need it decided for you months in advance.

Most importantly, you read the description of how this function actually runs and your first reaction was not "that sounds like a lot of process," it was "finally, a recruiting job built around the parts I'm actually good at." That's the person this role is for.

Why Manifest

Manifest Global is building the infrastructure for global human capital mobility, connecting students, schools, universities, and employers across 150+ countries. Our portfolio spans Cialfo (AI-powered college counseling, 2,000+ schools), BridgeU (university guidance for international schools globally), Kaaiser (trusted study abroad counseling since 1997 across India and Southeast Asia), and Explore (AI-powered university outreach, 1,000+ university partners). Together, we move talent across borders at scale. $700B flows annually in remittances from migrant workers. 85M workers will be missing from developed economies by 2030. We're building the operating system which changes that. $91M raised. Still early.

For this role specifically: Manifest is trying to prove a five-brand, multi-country hiring function can run better than companies many times its size. That only happens with recruiters who want to be excellent at the craft, not just keep the pipeline moving.
